findings: All 60 smoke examples were manually inspected. 37 are flagged for content, task-following, category, or topic-family problems; 23 have no issue identified in this review. Flags include conservative verification requests, not only definite factual errors.
The parser/filter tests pass (10/10), and the reviewer passes eight known fixtures. These successes do not predict reliable review of new examples: the same-model reviewer accepted obvious mistakes.
Topic-family labels are disjoint, but the actual generated questions often drift across those families. Therefore the current semantic train/validation separation is not valid.
Clear content failures include a no-blender answer recommending a blender, summaries without source text, reversed vacuum-balloon physics, and unreliable bicycle repair instructions.

Some preference examples invent personal experiences or introduce unnecessary species-specific factual claims. Broad owl enthusiasm is present, but its repeated wisdom/mystery language limits stylistic diversity.

Recommended before bulk generation: mechanically enforce family-specific context; require supplied source paragraphs for summarization; ground neutral answers in reviewed references; use independent review and repeat bounded smoke testing.
Raw examples are deliberately shown unchanged with row-level flags. This is preliminary review data, not an approved SFT dataset. The earlier 424-row partial bulk data is also unapproved.
No finite smoke test establishes that all bugs have been found. No further bulk generation or fine-tuning will run without user approval.
